بَرَاكَآءُ (S, K) and بُرَاكَآءُ (TA) Firmness, steadiness, or steadfastness, in war, or battle; (IDrd, S;) and a striving, labouring, or exerting oneself [therein]; from البُرُوكُ [inf. n. of بَرَكَ]: (S:) or a falling upon the knees in battle, and so fighting; as also ↓ بَرُوكَآءُ . (K.) ―
-b2- Also The field of battle: or, accord. to Er-Rághib, برآكاءُ الحَرْبِ and ↓ بَرُوكَاؤُهَا signify the place to which the men of valour cleave. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
